name: PGA National Resort
positioning: Golf resort in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, home of the Champion course and the Bear Trap, with a large spa and cottages designed by Serena & Lily
best_for: Golfers who want to play the course that hosts the PGA Tour's Cognizant Classic
Families and golf groups wanting a two-bedroom cottage with a kitchen

facts.text: The Palmer course is named after its designer, Arnold Palmer.
The Wee Bear is a par 3 course with holes ranging from 60 to 130 yards.
The Match course was designed with match play in mind.
Each cottage is a two-bedroom, two-bath retreat with outdoor space.
The cottages have a fully equipped kitchen and an en suite washer and dryer.
Guestrooms have a private balcony or terrace, with options for views of the pool, gardens and grounds.
The Presidential Suite has four balconies overlooking the pool and lake.
The spa has steam rooms, a sauna and a Himalayan Salt Chamber.
The spa has a whole-body cryotherapy chamber designed for single guests or couples.
The Sports & Racquet Club has 16 Har-Tru tennis courts, 12 pickleball courts and 2 pop tennis courts.
The resort has a kids club, the Banyan Buddies Kids Club.
The Butcher's Club, a steakhouse from Florida native chef Jeremy Ford, is a 2025 and 2026 Michelin-recommended restaurant.

highlights.text: The Champion course is home to the PGA Tour's Cognizant Classic and the Bear Trap, one of the most famed three-hole stretches in professional golf.
The resort has cottages designed by Serena & Lily.
The spa's signature Waters of the World experience features three mineral pools, including Dead Sea and Salies-de-Bearn pools, along with an outdoor hot tub.
The resort keeps four on-site beehives with almost 250,000 honeybees and offers a behind-the-scenes beekeeping experience.

considerations.text: The beaches, including a rare rock beach, are a short drive from the resort rather than on site; the concierge can arrange transportation.
Spa services are available for guests aged 18 and older.
WhataHotel notes the golf-focused resort may not appeal to non-golfers.
